subject: Post-call: Nimbus bake-off — proposed test roadmap & gap analysis
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Karen Park <karen@nimbusanalytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Post-call: Nimbus bake-off — proposed test roadmap & gap analysis

Hi Karen — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have alignment before we start running tests.

Recap of what we heard from you:
- Primary objective: pick a vendor for inference that lowers per-unit inference cost while maintaining sub-250ms p95 latency for the anonymized clinical-summary workload.
- Hyperscaler baseline: you will include the hyperscaler-managed endpoint (Tom Li) plus one additional third-party API for parity checks.
- Decision timing: target decision window ≈ 3 weeks (around 2026-07-20).

Proposed bake-off scope (short):
1) Latency SLA tests (p50/p95/p99) — 1k warm-up, stable 10k requests at peak QPS
2) Throughput / concurrency — sustained 200 concurrent streams, measure tail latencies
3) Cost modeling — tokenized-cost for 1M token-equivalent runs and estimated monthly cost at production QPS
4) Output quality — exact match + semantic similarity on the labeled evaluation set you shared
5) Failure modes & throttling — observe behavior under backend contention and KV-cache cold starts

Success criteria (proposal, please confirm):
- p95 latency <= 220ms on your anonymized clinical-summary set
- Quality: top-1 exact-match >= 78% OR semantic-similarity >= 0.88 (embedding cosine)
- Cost: < $X per 1M effective tokens (we'll flush exact numbers once we know concurrency profile)

Timeline (proposed):
- Today (06/30): confirm tests & success criteria + share test dataset (you mentioned a small anonymized slice)
- 07/01: Redwood provides updated test matrix, runbook, and a client container to run load tests
- 07/02 — 07/08: parallel runs against Hyperscaler + Redwood + 3rd party (we'll coordinate windows)
- 07/12: consolidated results and recommendation deck

Attachments: initial test matrix + gap-analysis stub (see attached file names).
[attachment: bakeoff-test-matrix.xlsx]
[attachment: redwood-hyperscaler-gap-analysis.pdf]

Ask from you: please confirm the success criteria above, share the anonymized test slice link and the preferred windows for cluster/tenant access. Also please confirm whether Tom (hyperscaler contact) will be invited to the test-run coordination calls.

I copied Ben and Vivek — Ben will own the run orchestration and Vivek will own the engineering analysis. I will coordinate timelines and executive updates.

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole

Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 13:45:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Nimbus bake-off — proposed test roadmap & gap analysis

Marissa — thanks for the clear summary. This looks right to me and the success criteria are a good starting point. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Dataset: attaching the anonymized slice (link below). It's a 2k-row sample derived from the clinical summary pipeline. Please ensure any logs or outputs are stored in your test bucket only.
- Sample link: https://s3.amazonaws.com/nimbus-test/samples/clinical-slice-2k.csv

2) Hyperscaler: Tom (cc'ed) will participate. We'll also invite our security reviewer if you need access-level details.

3) Decision date: internal stakeholders hope to have a recommendation by 2026-07-18, so earlier is better.

4) Data residency: can Redwood guarantee that test artifacts are deleted after 30 days? We need a short statement for our compliance thread.

We'll be available for the run window 07/02–07/06 afternoons (ET). Let me know if Redwood can run during that window.

Cheers,
Karen
Head of Data Platforms | Nimbus Analytics

Karen / team — quick technical follow-up and what we'll deliver by tomorrow morning: 

Deliverables (07/01 EOD):
- Updated bakeoff-test-matrix.xlsx with concrete test cases, runtimes, expected scripts per vendor. [attachment included]
- client-runbook.md: container image + exact invocation, env vars, and result artifact layout. [attachment included]
- A small load-generator container (we'll publish to your testing registry) and a sample config to reproduce runs locally.

Short notes on orchestration:
- We'll run each vendor in three phases: cold-start (no KV cache), warm-run (pre-warmed cache), and sustained-stream. That should surface both latency and cache-behavior differences.
- For cost comparatives we'll normalize to a 1M-token effective run — we need to know your avg tokens per request; if you share that, we can produce an apples-to-apples estimate.
- For the hyperscaler run we will coordinate with Tom to ensure identical prompt/temperature and model family where feasible.

Security/compliance: Redwood can delete test artifacts after 30 days. We'll also provide a signed attestation. (We'll send the attestation PDF once legal signs off.)

Attachments included: client-runbook.md, bakeoff-test-matrix.xlsx

Karen — thanks for the dataset link and for confirming windows. A couple of concrete engineering commitments and owners from Redwood: 

Owners & schedule:
- Ben will run orchestration and publish raw traces (Ben: lead)
- I will run the aggregation analysis and produce the latency/cost/quality deck (Vivek: lead)
- Marissa will coordinate scheduling and executive syncs (Marissa: lead)

Committed test windows (Redwood):
- 07/02 14:00–18:00 ET: Hyperscaler + Redwood parallel warm-run and cold-start comparisons
- 07/03 14:00–18:00 ET: Sustained throughput runs + failure-mode injection (rate throttles)

Engineering acceptance criteria (finalized before runs):
- p95 latency <= 220ms for the clinical-slice sample (goal p95 <= 200ms, stretch p95 <= 180ms)
- Throughput: sustain 200 concurrent streams with p95 <= 350ms during sustained-run
- Quality: semantic-similarity >= 0.88 on your labeled subset (we'll compute cosine on the embedding pairs)
- Cost: we'll report normalized cost per 1M tokens and provide a sensitivity table for concurrency and batch sizes

Access & pre-reqs we need from Nimbus today if possible:
- A short-lived test S3 token/manifest for the sample and a readonly bucket for result artifacts
- IAM contact for your infra team for a 30-min setup call (we'll only need minimal permissions to push logs to the results bucket)

Data retention: Redwood confirms deletion of test artifacts after 30 days and will provide a signed attestation.

I'll produce a short run-schedule doc and circulate it by EOD PST so we can lock the windows. Looking forward to running this.

— Vivek
